FellowShow · UX review

Make the next live action unmistakable

The workspace gives operators direct access to the tools they need. The biggest opportunity is to make staged content and live behavior easier to understand at a glance.

2 November 2026Web preview · 1280 × 720Off air

Walkthrough and evidence

I reviewed the available development preview without going live or changing saved content. The following steps show the states reached during the walkthrough.

  1. Songs · needs attention. Selected an existing song and examined its section and preview.
  2. Media · clear entry point. Switched to an empty Media workspace and checked what remained staged.
  3. Bible · setup blocked the flow. No Bible version was downloaded in this preview; the earlier song remained staged.
  4. Video Overlays · needs clearer labels. Reviewed the empty graphics workspace and keying controls.
  5. Notes, Displays, and Settings · incomplete. Notes had no content. Displays and Settings did not open in the browser preview, so their desktop dialogs were not assessed.

These screenshots cannot show real projector output, desktop-only dialogs, microphone permissions, or accessibility with assistive technology.

Findings

1

The staged item loses its context across workspaces

Live control Visible Medium

Evidence. After selecting a song while off air, switching to Media or Bible kept the song in Preview and left “Show on Live” available. See Media and Bible.

Problem. The active workspace does not identify the staged item as a song; its title is difficult to read inside the small preview.

Why it matters. An operator could mistake earlier content for the item they are about to show.

Suggestion. Keep the global preview, but label it with the source and title, such as “Staged · Song · Great is Thy faithfulness”. Show that label next to the live action at narrow widths.

2

A long song section makes the preview text very small

Song preparation Visible Medium

Evidence. In Song preparation, the selected first section includes a verse and chorus in one slide; the text is very small in the preview.

Problem. There is no visible indication that this section may be too dense for a presentation screen.

Why it matters. Readability depends on the display and viewing distance, so this section could be difficult for a congregation to read.

Suggestion. Flag dense sections and offer to split them into slides, with the original text preserved. Check the result on a real output before choosing a threshold.

3

Follow live does not explain its effect in the main view

Live control Visible Medium

Evidence. The song screen shows “Follow live” switched on. Its hover help says, “While this song is on air, selecting a section sends it to the screen.” Source inspection confirms that behavior.

Problem. The consequence is not visible beside the switch.

Why it matters. During a live song, an operator may expect a selection to change only Preview.

Suggestion. Show “Selecting a section goes live” beside the control when the song is on air, and explain the behavior on first use.

4

Keying modes rely on unexplained abbreviations

Video overlays Visible Medium

Evidence. Video Overlays presents “DSK” and “CMK” in a segmented control. The mode descriptions are available in the underlying controls but are not visible in this view.

Problem. The labels do not explain the available black and green background options.

Why it matters. An operator unfamiliar with the terms has to guess or look for help.

Suggestion. Add a short explanation in a help popover or use labels such as “Black key (DSK)” and “Green key (CMK)”. Verify the wording with the actual output workflow.

5

Some song titles need a character-encoding check

Song library Needs verification Medium

Evidence. The song list includes titles with digits and punctuation, including “Nyame ne y1n w4 h4”. The source and intended encoding were not verified.

Risk. If these are legacy encoded characters, operators may struggle to recognize or search the songs.

Why verify. The characters could also be intentional in the source library; changing them automatically could damage the original text.

Suggestion. Inspect the source library and offer an optional conversion preview, keeping the original alongside the proposed text.

6

The Media empty state offers a clear next action

Empty states Visible Working well

Evidence. Media explains that there is no presentation media and presents a prominent “Import media” button.

Why it works. A new operator can see how to begin without searching a menu.

What to preserve. Keep the direct import action and short list of supported content types.

Suggested order

  1. Make the staged source and title visible wherever the live action appears.
  2. Add a way to detect and split dense song sections, then check a real output.
  3. Explain Follow live and the overlay keying modes in the workspace.
  4. Verify the song library encoding before offering any conversion.

After that, check a populated Notes and Media workflow, scripture setup, the display dialogs, microphone permissions, keyboard access, and actual output in the desktop app.
